node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/01-directives/use-cache.md 1 --- 2 title: use cache 3 description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application. 4 related: 5 title: Related 6 description: View related API references. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private 9 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 10 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife 11 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers 12 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 13 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife 14 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 15 --- 16 17 The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async. 18 19 > **Good to know:** 20 > 21 > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern. 22 > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees. 23 > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 24 25 ## Usage 26 27 `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file: 28 29 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 30 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 31 32 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 33 cacheComponents: true, 34 } 35 36 export default nextConfig 37 ``` 38 39 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 40 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 41 const nextConfig = { 42 cacheComponents: true, 43 } 44 45 module.exports = nextConfig 46 ``` 47 48 Then, add `use cache` at the function, component, or file level. Cached functions and components must be async: 49 50 ```tsx 51 // Function level 52 export async function getData() { 53 'use cache' 54 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 55 const data = await res.json() 56 return data 57 } 58 59 // Component level 60 export async function MyComponent() { 61 'use cache' 62 return <> 63 } 64 ``` 65 66 When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async: 67 68 ```tsx 69 // File level 70 'use cache' 71 72 export default async function Page() { 73 // ... 74 } 75 ``` 76 77 ## How `use cache` works 78 79 ### Cache keys 80 81 A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes: 82 83 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes. 84 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase 85 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments 86 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement 87 88 When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key. 89 90 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 91 async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) { 92 const getData = async (filter: string) => { 93 'use cache' 94 // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument) 95 const res = await fetch( 96 `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}` 97 ) 98 return res.json() 99 } 100 101 return getData('active') 102 } 103 ``` 104 105 In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries. 106 107 > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key. 108 109 ### Cache output 110 111 A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts. 112 113 Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation). 114 115 ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts" 116 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 117 118 export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) { 119 'use cache' 120 cacheLife('hours') 121 122 const orders = await getOrders(accountId) 123 const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId) 124 125 return { orders, totals } 126 } 127 128 export async function getOrders(accountId: string) { 129 'use cache' 130 cacheLife('hours') 131 132 return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } }) 133 } 134 135 export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) { 136 return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } }) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it. 141 142 Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there. 143 144 With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds. 145 146 ## Serialization 147 148 Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable. 149 150 For a complete reference, see: 151 152 - [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization 153 - [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization 154 155 > **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/cacheLife.md 1 --- 2 title: cacheLife 3 description: Learn how to use the cacheLife function to set the cache expiration time for a cached function or component. 4 related: 5 title: Related 6 description: View related API references. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 9 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache 10 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 11 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 12 --- 13 14 The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component. 15 16 ## Usage 17 18 ### Basic setup 19 20 To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file: 21 22 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 23 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 24 25 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 26 cacheComponents: true, 27 } 28 29 export default nextConfig 30 ``` 31 32 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 33 const nextConfig = { 34 cacheComponents: true, 35 } 36 37 module.exports = nextConfig 38 ``` 39 40 `cacheLife` can only be used within a cache directive scope. 41 42 Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component. 43 44 `cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. 45 46 > **Good to know**: 47 > 48 > - We recommend setting a `cacheLife` in every `use cache` scope so its behavior is clear at the call site. Omitting it leaves the lifetime implicit (the `default` profile applies), which makes it harder to reason about, for example in [nested cached scopes](#nested-caching-behavior). 49 > - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. 50 > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. 51 52 ### Using preset profiles 53 54 Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: 55 56 - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) 57 - How often fresh content is generated on the server 58 - When old content expires completely 59 60 Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: 61 62 - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) 63 - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) 64 - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) 65 - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) 66 - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) 67 - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) 68 69 Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 72 'use cache' 73 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 74 75 export default async function BlogPage() { 76 cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily 77 78 const posts = await getBlogPosts() 79 return
{/* render posts */}
80 } 81 ``` 82 83 The profile name tells Next.js how to cache the entire function's output. If you don't call `cacheLife`, the `default` profile is used. See [preset cache profiles](#preset-cache-profiles) for timing details. 84 85 ## Reference 86 87 ### Cache profile properties 88 89 Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties: 90 91 - **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data without checking the server 92 - **[`revalidate`](#revalidate)**: After this time, the next request will trigger a background refresh 93 - **[`expire`](#expire)**: After this time with no requests, the next one waits for fresh content 94 95 #### `stale` 96 97 **Client-side:** How long the client can use cached data without checking the server. 98 99 During this time, the client-side router displays cached content immediately without any network request. After this period expires, the router must check with the server on the next navigation or request. This provides instant page loads from the client cache, but data may be outdated. 100 101 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `stale` value (5 minutes, see [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) 102 - Also determines whether the content can be part of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). See [Prerendering behavior](#prerendering-behavior). 103 104 ```tsx 105 cacheLife({ stale: 300 }) // 5 minutes 106 ``` 107 108 #### `revalidate` 109 110 How often the server regenerates cached content in the background. 111 112 - When a request arrives after this period, the server: 113 1. 4  	related:

13 	---
14 	
15 	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
16 	
17 	## Usage
18 	
19 	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
20 	
21 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
22 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
23 	
24 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
25 	  cacheComponents: true,
26 	}
27 	
28 	export default nextConfig
29 	```
30 	
31 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
32 	const nextConfig = {
33 	  cacheComponents: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	module.exports = nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
40 	
41 	```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
42 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
43 	
44 	export async function getData() {
45 	  'use cache'
46 	  cacheTag('my-data')
47 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
48 	  const data = await res.json()
49 	  return data
50 	}
51 	```
52 	
53 	```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
54 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
55 	
56 	export async function getData() {
57 	  'use cache'
58 	  cacheTag('my-data')
59 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
60 	  const data = await res.json()
61 	  return data
62 	}
63 	```
64 	
65 	You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
66 	
67 	- Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
68 	- Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
69 	
70 	For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
71 	
72 	```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
73 	'use server'
74 	
75 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
76 	
77 	export default async function submit() {
78 	  await addPost()
79 	  updateTag('my-data')
80 	}
81 	```
82 	
83 	```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
84 	'use server'
85 	
86 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
87 	
88 	export default async function submit() {
89 	  await addPost()
90 	  updateTag('my-data')
91 	}
92 	```
93 	
94 	## Good to know
95 	
96 	- **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
97 	- **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
98 	
99 	```tsx
100	cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')
101	```
102	
103	- **Limits**: A single `cacheTag()` call accepts up to 128 tags, each with a maximum length of 256 characters. Tags longer than 256 characters are skipped, and any tags past the 128th in one call are dropped. Both cases log a console warning.
104	
105	## Examples
106	
107	### Tagging components or functions
108	
109	Tag your cached data by calling `cacheTag` within a cached function or component:
110	
111	```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
112	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
113	
114	interface BookingsProps {
115	  type: string
116	}
117	
118	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
119	  'use cache'
120	  cacheTag('bookings-data')
121	
122	  async function getBookingsData() {
123	    const response = await fetch(
124	      `https://api.example.com/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`
125	    )
126	    const data = await response.json()
127	    return data
128	  }
129	
130	  return //...
131	}
132	```
133	
134	```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" switcher
135	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
136	
137	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }) {

140

142	    const response = await fetch(

144	    )
145	    const data = await response.json()
146	    return data
147	  }
148	
149	  return //...
150	}
151	```
152	
153	### Creating tags from external data
154	
155	You can use the data returned from an async function to tag the cache entry.
